explanation: A=T=30%, leaving 40% for G+C; because G=C, each is 20%.

distractorExplanations.A: Guanine pairs with cytosine, not necessarily with the adenine percentage.
distractorExplanations.C: That is the nonadenine fraction and includes three bases.
distractorExplanations.D: Forty percent is the combined G+C fraction, not guanine alone.

source.title: Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry
source.excerpt: Source-supported mechanism, paraphrased: A=T=30%, leaving 40% for G+C; because G=C, each is 20%.

subject: biochemistry
learningObjective: Apply Primer requirement within DNA structure, replication and repair.
prompt: A DNA polymerase has a DNA template and dNTPs but no primer. Why can it not start an ordinary new strand de novo?

options.text: It requires an RNA template instead of a DNA template
It can initiate from a 5′ phosphate without a 3′ hydroxyl
It consumes ribonucleoside triphosphates rather than dNTPs
It requires an existing 3′ hydroxyl to extend

explanation: Replicative DNA polymerases add nucleotides to a pre-existing 3′OH supplied by a primer; primase can initiate the RNA primer.

distractorExplanations.A: Ordinary replicative DNA polymerases copy DNA templates.
distractorExplanations.B: Extension specifically requires a 3′OH acceptor.
distractorExplanations.C: Replicative DNA synthesis uses dNTPs; lack of a primer remains the block.

source.title: Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry
source.excerpt: Source-supported mechanism, paraphrased: Replicative DNA polymerases add nucleotides to a pre-existing 3′OH supplied by a primer; primase can initiate the RNA primer.

subject: biochemistry
learningObjective: Apply Repair pathway distinction within DNA structure, replication and repair.
prompt: A uracil base appears in DNA after cytosine deamination. Which repair strategy most directly removes the abnormal base first?

options.text: Base-excision repair initiated by a DNA glycosylase
Nucleotide-excision repair exclusively for every uracil
Homologous recombination as the routine single-base mechanism

explanation: A uracil-DNA glycosylase initiates base-excision repair by removing the inappropriate base, followed by repair of the abasic site.

distractorExplanations.B: NER classically removes bulky helix-distorting lesions rather than being the primary uracil pathway.
distractorExplanations.C: HR is especially relevant to double-strand-break repair.
distractorExplanations.D: Telomerase extends chromosome ends rather than removing uracil lesions.

source.title: Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry
source.excerpt: Source-supported mechanism, paraphrased: A uracil-DNA glycosylase initiates base-excision repair by removing the inappropriate base, followed by repair of the abasic site.

subject: biochemistry
learningObjective: Apply Template sequence within RNA, transcription and processing.
prompt: RNA polymerase reads the DNA template 3′-TACGGA-5′. Which RNA sequence is produced?
explanation: RNA is synthesized 5′→3′ complementary and antiparallel to the DNA template: T→A, A→U, C→G, G→C.

distractorExplanations.A: This reverses the correct transcript while still labeling it 5′→3′.
distractorExplanations.B: This resembles the template rather than its complementary RNA.
distractorExplanations.D: RNA uses uracil instead of thymine.

source.title: Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry
source.excerpt: Source-supported mechanism, paraphrased: RNA is synthesized 5′→3′ complementary and antiparallel to the DNA template: T→A, A→U, C→G, G→C.

subject: biochemistry
learningObjective: Apply Splice-site variant within RNA, transcription and processing.
prompt: A mutation disrupts a splice donor site without changing the encoded amino-acid codons in nearby exons. How can it still cause disease?

options.text: All noncoding positions are incapable of affecting expression
It can alter exon joining or intron removal in the mature mRNA
It must be harmless whenever the reading frame of genomic exons is unchanged
It can alter only DNA replication, never RNA maturation

explanation: Splice-site mutations can cause intron retention or exon skipping, changing reading frame, protein sequence, or transcript abundance.

distractorExplanations.A: Splice signals are essential functional sequences even when noncoding.
distractorExplanations.C: Exon skipping or intron retention can alter the mature transcript despite intact genomic coding triplets.
distractorExplanations.D: Splice signals directly govern pre-mRNA processing.

source.title: Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry
source.excerpt: Source-supported mechanism, paraphrased: Splice-site mutations can cause intron retention or exon skipping, changing reading frame, protein sequence, or transcript abundance.

subject: biochemistry
learningObjective: Apply Polymerase specialization within RNA, transcription and processing.
prompt: A nucleus retains RNA polymerase I and III activity but loses polymerase II activity. Which synthesis is most directly reduced?
explanation: RNA polymerase II transcribes protein-coding genes into pre-mRNA and also produces certain noncoding RNAs.

distractorExplanations.B: polymerase I makes the major rRNA precursor.
distractorExplanations.C: polymerase III makes tRNA.
distractorExplanations.D: polymerase III makes 5S rRNA.

source.title: Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry
source.excerpt: Source-supported mechanism, paraphrased: RNA polymerase II transcribes protein-coding genes into pre-mRNA and also produces certain noncoding RNAs.

subject: biochemistry
learningObjective: Apply Mischarged tRNA experiment within Translation.
prompt: A tRNA with an anticodon for phenylalanine is experimentally charged with alanine. If it escapes quality control, what does the ribosome use to choose the mRNA codon?

options.text: The amino-acid side chain alone, forcing an alanine codon
The mature protein’s folded binding pocket
The amino acid’s original synthetase-binding site after it has detached
The tRNA anticodon, potentially inserting alanine at a phenylalanine codon

explanation: Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases normally ensure correct charging; the ribosome mainly checks codon-anticodon pairing, so a mischarged tRNA can insert the wrong amino acid.

distractorExplanations.A: Codon recognition primarily depends on anticodon pairing, not direct reading of the attached side chain.
distractorExplanations.B: The final fold does not specify the immediate decoding event.
distractorExplanations.C: The ribosome primarily decodes the anticodon, not a remembered synthetase interaction.

source.title: Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry
source.excerpt: Source-supported mechanism, paraphrased: Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases normally ensure correct charging; the ribosome mainly checks codon-anticodon pairing, so a mischarged tRNA can insert the wrong amino acid.

subject: biochemistry
learningObjective: Apply Peptide-transfer direction within Translation.
prompt: During elongation, peptidyl transferase transfers the growing peptide from which location to which acceptor?

options.text: From P-site tRNA to E-site deacylated tRNA
From A-site tRNA back to the carboxyl group on P-site aminoacyl-tRNA
From the ribosomal large subunit to a free amino acid in solution
From P-site tRNA to the amino group on A-site aminoacyl-tRNA

explanation: The amino group of the A-site aminoacyl-tRNA attacks the peptide linked to P-site tRNA, extending the chain at its carboxyl end.

distractorExplanations.A: The acceptor is the A-site aminoacyl-tRNA.
distractorExplanations.B: The growing chain moves from P-site to A-site tRNA, not in the opposite direction.
distractorExplanations.C: The chain is linked to tRNA and the incoming amino acid is also tRNA-bound.

source.title: Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry
source.excerpt: Source-supported mechanism, paraphrased: The amino group of the A-site aminoacyl-tRNA attacks the peptide linked to P-site tRNA, extending the chain at its carboxyl end.

subject: biochemistry
learningObjective: Apply Frameshift comparison within Translation.
prompt: Which coding-sequence deletion is most likely to shift all downstream reading-frame assignments?
explanation: A deletion not divisible by three changes the grouping of downstream codons; one nucleotide therefore creates a frameshift.

distractorExplanations.A: Three bases remove one codon while usually preserving the downstream frame.
distractorExplanations.C: Nine bases correspond to three full codons and usually preserve the frame.
distractorExplanations.D: Six bases correspond to two full codons and usually preserve the frame.

source.title: Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry
source.excerpt: Source-supported mechanism, paraphrased: A deletion not divisible by three changes the grouping of downstream codons; one nucleotide therefore creates a frameshift.

subject: biochemistry
learningObjective: Apply Two-signal integration within Gene regulation.
prompt: An E.coli culture has lactose available but abundant glucose. Why is lac transcription less than its fully induced level?

options.text: The glucose signal keeps cAMP-CAP at maximum activation
Lactose can induce the operon only after all DNA replication stops
Low cAMP limits CAP-mediated positive activation despite reduced repressor binding

explanation: Lactose relieves negative repression, but glucose lowers cAMP and therefore CAP activation; both signals are needed for maximal lac expression.

distractorExplanations.A: Glucose availability lowers cAMP-dependent positive activation.
distractorExplanations.B: Induction depends on regulatory signals, not complete replication arrest.
distractorExplanations.C: Allolactose reduces repressor binding to the operator.

source.title: Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry
source.excerpt: Source-supported mechanism, paraphrased: Lactose relieves negative repression, but glucose lowers cAMP and therefore CAP activation; both signals are needed for maximal lac expression.

subject: biochemistry
learningObjective: Apply Cis-element experiment within Gene regulation.
prompt: A mutation damages an enhancer next to one gene but leaves a diffusible transcription factor intact. Why is the effect described as cis-acting?

options.text: It can regulate only RNA stability after transcription
The enhancer is a protein that diffuses to every chromosome
It is a diffusible factor that binds any gene with no sequence preference
It is tied to the regulatory DNA associated with that gene

explanation: A cis-regulatory element acts as a DNA site associated with its target, whereas trans-acting factors can diffuse and bind multiple appropriate sites.

distractorExplanations.A: Enhancers act at DNA transcriptional regulation rather than being limited to mRNA stability.
distractorExplanations.B: Enhancers are DNA sequences rather than diffusible proteins.
distractorExplanations.C: That does not describe a cis DNA element and ignores sequence-specific regulation.

source.title: Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry
source.excerpt: Source-supported mechanism, paraphrased: A cis-regulatory element acts as a DNA site associated with its target, whereas trans-acting factors can diffuse and bind multiple appropriate sites.

subject: biochemistry
learningObjective: Apply MicroRNA effect within Gene regulation.
prompt: A microRNA pairs with a target mRNA in a silencing complex. Which result is most plausible?

options.text: Obligatory increased transcription of the target in every case
Direct removal of introns from the genomic DNA
Reduced translation and/or increased degradation of that mRNA
Increased ribosome loading as its universal effect

explanation: MicroRNAs guide complexes to complementary mRNAs and commonly reduce protein production through translational repression and/or mRNA destabilization.

distractorExplanations.A: MicroRNA action generally suppresses target expression posttranscriptionally.
distractorExplanations.B: MicroRNAs act on RNA expression rather than excising genomic introns.
distractorExplanations.D: MicroRNA action commonly suppresses rather than universally enhances translation.

source.title: Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry
source.excerpt: Source-supported mechanism, paraphrased: MicroRNAs guide complexes to complementary mRNAs and commonly reduce protein production through translational repression and/or mRNA destabilization.

subject: biochemistry
learningObjective: Apply Ideal PCR arithmetic within Biotechnology.
prompt: One double-stranded DNA target undergoes 5 ideal PCR cycles with exact doubling each cycle. How many double-stranded copies result?
explanation: Under ideal complete doubling, copy number is N0×2^n=1×2^5=32; real reactions eventually become less efficient.

distractorExplanations.A: The count is 2^5, not 5 squared.
distractorExplanations.B: The increase is exponential, not one copy per cycle.
distractorExplanations.C: Doubling is repeated each cycle rather than applied once to the cycle count.

source.title: Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry
source.excerpt: Source-supported mechanism, paraphrased: Under ideal complete doubling, copy number is N0×2^n=1×2^5=32; real reactions eventually become less efficient.

subject: biochemistry
learningObjective: Apply Primer orientation within Biotechnology.
prompt: For PCR amplification across a target region, how should the two primers be oriented?

options.text: Their 5′ ends must be covalently joined before the first cycle
Both must bind the exact same sequence on the same strand
Both 3′ ends point away from the target
Their 3′ ends point toward the region to be copied on opposite strands

explanation: DNA polymerase extends each primer from its 3′ end, so the primers must face inward on opposite template strands.

distractorExplanations.A: Primers function separately and need not be ligated to each other.
distractorExplanations.B: Opposing-strand priming is needed for exponential amplification of the interval.
distractorExplanations.C: Extension away from the target does not amplify the intended intervening region exponentially.

source.title: Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry
source.excerpt: Source-supported mechanism, paraphrased: DNA polymerase extends each primer from its 3′ end, so the primers must face inward on opposite template strands.

subject: biochemistry
learningObjective: Apply Negative-control interpretation within Biotechnology.
prompt: A no-template PCR control gives a band of the same size as the expected target. What is the most immediate concern?

options.text: The patient necessarily has a homozygous deletion
Contamination of reagents or reaction setup with target DNA
The target has been proven absent from all sample reactions

explanation: A no-template control should not generate the target product; a matching band raises concern for contamination and undermines interpretation.

distractorExplanations.A: A target-size product in the negative control is a warning, not validation.
distractorExplanations.B: The control contains no patient template, so this cannot establish that genotype.
distractorExplanations.D: A contaminated negative control makes sample interpretation less reliable, not proof of target absence.

source.title: Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry
source.excerpt: Source-supported mechanism, paraphrased: A no-template control should not generate the target product; a matching band raises concern for contamination and undermines interpretation.

subject: biochemistry
learningObjective: Apply Library tissue specificity within Biotechnology.
prompt: Why do liver and muscle cDNA libraries differ even when their cells have essentially the same genome?

options.text: cDNA synthesis routinely copies only introns
cDNA libraries contain only mitochondrial DNA
Each tissue normally has a completely different chromosome set
They reflect different mRNAs expressed in each tissue

explanation: cDNA is made from the mRNA population present when sampled, so tissue-specific gene expression produces different library representation.

distractorExplanations.A: Mature mRNA-derived cDNA generally lacks removed introns.
distractorExplanations.B: They are made from RNA transcripts, not exclusively mitochondrial DNA.
distractorExplanations.C: Most somatic tissues share the same genome despite different expression.

source.title: Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry
source.excerpt: Source-supported mechanism, paraphrased: cDNA is made from the mRNA population present when sampled, so tissue-specific gene expression produces different library representation.

subject: biochemistry
learningObjective: Apply Genomic-library choice within Biotechnology.
prompt: A researcher needs introns and upstream genomic regulatory sequences for a gene. Which library is the better starting point?

options.text: A cDNA library prepared from mature mRNA
A library of short mature mRNA fragments only

explanation: A genomic library contains genomic DNA, including introns and regulatory regions; a cDNA library primarily represents processed transcripts.

distractorExplanations.A: Mature mRNA-derived cDNA lacks removed introns and genomic upstream regulatory DNA.
distractorExplanations.B: Protein-expression arrays do not supply genomic introns and promoters.
distractorExplanations.C: Processed transcript fragments omit the needed genomic sequences.

source.title: Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry
source.excerpt: Source-supported mechanism, paraphrased: A genomic library contains genomic DNA, including introns and regulatory regions; a cDNA library primarily represents processed transcripts.

subject: biochemistry
learningObjective: Apply Restriction-fragment inference within Biotechnology.
prompt: A point mutation abolishes one restriction site within a 1000 bp fragment previously cut into 400 bp and 600 bp pieces. What mutant fragment is expected after that digest?
explanation: Removing the internal restriction site leaves the original 1000 bp fragment uncut at that location.

distractorExplanations.B: A new cleavage position has not been introduced in the scenario.
distractorExplanations.C: Loss of the site prevents separation into the original two pieces.
distractorExplanations.D: That shorter fragment required the site that is now absent.

source.title: Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry
source.excerpt: Source-supported mechanism, paraphrased: Removing the internal restriction site leaves the original 1000 bp fragment uncut at that location.

subject: biochemistry
learningObjective: Apply Expression-level separation within Biotechnology.
prompt: A gene has normal DNA copy number, low mRNA abundance, and low protein abundance. Which test directly measures the low RNA component?

options.text: Restriction mapping of genomic DNA alone

explanation: Northern blotting detects specific RNA transcripts, allowing assessment of transcript abundance and size.

distractorExplanations.A: Restriction mapping does not directly measure mRNA abundance.
distractorExplanations.B: Western blot detects protein rather than the transcript itself.
distractorExplanations.D: Southern blot detects DNA rather than RNA abundance.

source.title: Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry
source.excerpt: Source-supported mechanism, paraphrased: Northern blotting detects specific RNA transcripts, allowing assessment of transcript abundance and size.

subject: biochemistry
learningObjective: Apply Selectable marker purpose within Biotechnology.
prompt: Why does a plasmid cloning vector commonly contain an antibiotic-resistance gene?

options.text: To guarantee the inserted gene is expressed in every orientation
To make the plasmid independent of an origin of replication
To ensure every surviving cell contains the intended insert in the correct orientation
To select cells that acquired the plasmid

explanation: A selectable marker permits enrichment of cells carrying the plasmid; successful selection alone does not prove the insert is correct.

distractorExplanations.A: Selection for the vector does not guarantee correct orientation or expression.
distractorExplanations.B: A selectable marker does not replace the replication origin.
distractorExplanations.C: Resistance selects vector-bearing cells but does not by itself verify insert identity/orientation.

source.title: Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry
source.excerpt: Source-supported mechanism, paraphrased: A selectable marker permits enrichment of cells carrying the plasmid; successful selection alone does not prove the insert is correct.

subject: biochemistry
learningObjective: Apply Chain-termination chemistry within Biotechnology.
prompt: A nucleotide analog has a base and 5′ triphosphate but lacks a 3′ hydroxyl. Once incorporated, why does elongation stop?

options.text: It cannot pair with any base under any circumstances
The next phosphodiester bond lacks the required 3′OH acceptor
It cleaves the template at every guanine
It forces the polymerase to synthesize 3′→5′

explanation: DNA extension requires a free 3′ hydroxyl on the terminal nucleotide; a dideoxynucleotide lacks this group and terminates the chain.

distractorExplanations.A: Dideoxynucleotides can pair and be incorporated.
distractorExplanations.C: Chain termination is not template cleavage.
distractorExplanations.D: Polymerase direction is not reversed by chain termination.

source.title: Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry
source.excerpt: Source-supported mechanism, paraphrased: DNA extension requires a free 3′ hydroxyl on the terminal nucleotide; a dideoxynucleotide lacks this group and terminates the chain.

subject: biochemistry
learningObjective: Apply Hybridization discrimination within Biotechnology.
prompt: Why does increasing hybridization stringency help an allele-specific probe distinguish a perfect match from a single-base mismatch?

options.text: It covalently ligates every matching probe-target pair
It corrects the mismatched nucleotide by proofreading
The mismatched duplex is less stable and dissociates preferentially
It ensures even completely unrelated sequences stay bound

explanation: Stringent conditions destabilize imperfect base pairing more than a matched duplex, improving sequence discrimination within an appropriate assay range.

distractorExplanations.A: Hybridization remains based on noncovalent base pairing.
distractorExplanations.B: Hybridization stringency is not a repair mechanism.
distractorExplanations.D: Higher stringency favors more complementary, not unrelated, duplexes.

source.title: Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry
source.excerpt: Source-supported mechanism, paraphrased: Stringent conditions destabilize imperfect base pairing more than a matched duplex, improving sequence discrimination within an appropriate assay range.

subject: biochemistry
learningObjective: Apply Normality calculation within Laboratory principles and tests.
prompt: A 20.0 mL acid aliquot requires 15.0 mL of 0.100 N NaOH at equivalence. What is the acid normality?
explanation: Using NacidVacid=NbaseVbase gives Nacid=(0.100×15.0)/20.0=0.0750 N.

distractorExplanations.A: Equal normality would require equal equivalent volumes in this setup.
distractorExplanations.B: The volume and normality relationship gives 0.0750 N, not 0.300 N.
distractorExplanations.C: That reverses the volume ratio.

source.title: Biochemistry Retake Review — teacher foundations and practical curriculum
source.excerpt: Source-supported mechanism, paraphrased: Using NacidVacid=NbaseVbase gives Nacid=(0.100×15.0)/20.0=0.0750 N.

subject: biochemistry
learningObjective: Apply Dilution correction within Laboratory principles and tests.
prompt: A serum sample is diluted 1 volume sample plus 4 volumes diluent. The diluted sample measures 18 units/L within the linear range. What is the original concentration?
explanation: The total dilution factor is 5, so original concentration=18×5=90 units/L.

distractorExplanations.A: There are 5 total volumes, not 4.
distractorExplanations.B: The original concentration is higher, not lower, than the diluted concentration.
distractorExplanations.C: This omits correction for dilution.

source.title: Biochemistry Retake Review — teacher foundations and practical curriculum
source.excerpt: Source-supported mechanism, paraphrased: The total dilution factor is 5, so original concentration=18×5=90 units/L.

subject: biochemistry
learningObjective: Apply Retention-factor calculation within Laboratory principles and tests.
prompt: On a TLC plate, a solute travels 3 cm and the solvent front travels 8 cm from the origin. What is the Rf?
explanation: Rf=distance traveled by solute/distance traveled by solvent front=3/8=0.375.

distractorExplanations.A: Rf is a ratio, not the product of distances.
distractorExplanations.C: That inverts solute and solvent distances; valid Rf cannot exceed 1 here.
distractorExplanations.D: The difference in distances is not Rf.
